topic_inventory.title: Market Correction Analysis & Technical Outlook
topic_inventory.summary: Analysis of the recent sharp market drop, evaluating potential causes (dismissing war/rate hikes, favoring institutional rebalancing), assessing technical damage (break below 60-day MA), and outlining a cautious, selective trading strategy.

topic_inventory.title: Portfolio Strategy & Cross-Market Allocation
topic_inventory.summary: Description of recent portfolio adjustments: rotating through Taiwan market themes, selling underperformers/Tesla to fund SpaceX, trimming semiconductor winners, and planning to buy into weakened US tech giants (Google, Apple) in anticipation of a rotation to applications.

topic_inventory.title: Apple Price Hike & Consumer Market Dynamics
topic_inventory.summary: Analysis of Apple's decision to raise prices on existing products, contrasting enterprise (AI) vs. consumer demand elasticity, emphasizing Apple's brand premium and the need to watch sales data to gauge consumer acceptance.

topic_inventory.title: Investment Psychology & Behavioral Observations
topic_inventory.summary: Observations on the wealth effect paradox (rising markets suppress spending due to high opportunity cost), the 'lose it不如 spend it' mentality during volatility, and the near-universal inability to exit a bull market.

topic_inventory.title: Performance Review & Market Anomaly
topic_inventory.summary: Review of exceptional personal and investment performance in H1 2026, driven by a bull market and the unique phenomenon of 'disposition stocks' (處置股) becoming high-flyers, ironically benefiting from trading lock-ups.

topic_inventory.title: Business & Investment Philosophy
topic_inventory.summary: Philosophy on business partnerships and venture investing: aversion to complex ownership structures, preference for being the sole/majority investor to maintain control and simplicity, and viewing local community investments as a form of social support.

cross_topic_links.description: The analysis of the market correction (Topic 1) directly informs the portfolio strategy (Topic 2), specifically the decision to be cautious on broken sectors and to look for opportunities in weakened tech giants.

The discussion on Apple's price hike (Topic 3) explicitly contrasts the demand dynamics of the consumer market with the uncritical, strategic demand from tech giants in the AI supply chain, a point also raised in the market correction analysis regarding shareholder impatience.

The behavioral observation about the wealth effect suppressing spending (Topic 4) is cited as a potential future support for consumer price hikes (like Apple's) if market volatility triggers a 'spend it' mentality.

corrections_or_contradictions.description: The host admits to a trading error: buying too early during a presumed rebound and getting '套在一個他媽日內的高點'. This is a correction of his own market timing judgment.

cross_episode_candidate_records.title: The 'Disposition Stock' Anomaly in Bull Markets
cross_episode_candidate_records.summary: A specific market mechanism in Taiwan where stocks placed under trading restrictions (處置股) can paradoxically become momentum plays ('越關越大尾'), leading to outsized gains for locked-in holders. This is a structural quirk that can significantly impact performance.

cross_episode_candidate_records.title: Enterprise vs. Consumer Demand Framework for Pricing Power
cross_episode_candidate_records.summary: A framework for analyzing companies based on their end customer: strategic, budget-insensitive enterprise buyers (e.g., AI tech giants) vs. price-sensitive general consumers. This explains divergent market reactions to similar news (price hikes) and is crucial for risk assessment.

cross_episode_candidate_records.title: Tech Giant Shareholder Impatience with AI Capex
cross_episode_candidate_records.summary: An emerging risk scenario where shareholders of major tech companies, seeing poor stock performance despite massive capital outflows to suppliers, may pressure management to slow AI infrastructure spending, potentially derailing the supplier investment thesis.

strategy_reason: The episode contains multiple distinct, valuable investment reasoning threads (market analysis, portfolio strategy, consumer analysis, behavioral finance). However, there is no single, overarching central theme that unifies them; they are separate discussions. A 'light_consolidation' effectively inventories these topics, identifies their relationships, and extracts reusable analytical frameworks without forcing a non-existent episode-level narrative.
